key_insight: LuxRemix decomposes complex indoor illumination from a single multi-view capture into individual light sources using a generative image-based model, enabling independent editing of each source’s on/off state, chromaticity, and intensity while preserving multi-view consistency.
problem_solved: Interactive, per-light editing and realistic relighting of indoor scenes from limited multi-view captures is hard because indoor illumination is complex and entangled across views and surfaces.
method: Generative image-based light decomposition that factorizes scene illumination into constituent light sources from a single multi-view capture.
Per-source control interface allowing manipulation of state (on/off), chromaticity, and intensity for each decomposed light.
Multi-view lighting harmonization to ensure edits remain consistent and photorealistic across all views.
impact: Enables realistic, fine-grained lighting edits for AR/VR, interior design, and content creation without full scene relighting pipelines; simplifies dataset capture and interactive editing workflows for researchers and practitioners.
visual_elements: Before/after render of an indoor scene showing individual lights turned on/off or recolored
Pipeline diagram: multi-view capture -> generative decomposition -> per-light controls -> harmonized multi-view output
Per-light visualization (mask + color/intensity sliders) to show isolated contribution of each light source
Multi-view consistency comparison (several camera angles) to demonstrate harmonization
paper_title: LuxRemix: Lighting Decomposition and Remixing for Indoor Scenes
paper_authors: Ruofan Liang, Norman Müller, Ethan Weber, Duncan Zauss, Nandita Vijaykumar
